context_prefix_rationale: TSK_PRCH_* is consumed by SF_PORCH_CEILING_EXT_NC_v1 (31 tasks). Using PCRP_ (Porch Ceiling RePaint) eliminates all ID collisions. Verified: TSK_PCRP_* has zero existing usage in the codebase. MOD_PCRP_* also has zero existing usage. Pattern follows established convention: PC = porch ceiling, RP = repaint. Similar to SFRP_ pattern for soffit repaint.
scope_summary: Combined condition assessment + prep + prime + finish repaint spec for previously painted exterior porch ceiling surfaces on residential homes. Covers 2 substrate material types (wood T&G/beadboard/plywood, fiber cement) inherited from NC spec. NO vinyl substrate (porch ceilings are not manufactured in vinyl). Porch ceiling is the underside of a covered porch/portico/breezeway roof — ALL work is overhead, with same productivity penalty as soffit. Key differences from soffit RP: (1) spray ALWAYS eligible (no vent type constraint — porch ceilings have no vents), (2) beadboard panel type added (same 1.20x modifier as T&G), (3) lower access height than soffit (typically 8-10 ft walkable step ladder vs soffit 16+ ft), (4) more ceiling-mounted fixtures (fans, pendant lights, recessed cans), (5) porch furniture cover/removal instead of landscape protection, (6) mildew/algae is the #1 degradation concern (sheltered damp overhead surface). SF-based measurement. QT2-QT4 (QT5 excluded — porch ceiling is a field surface, not fine-finish millwork). Single mobilization: assess + prep + prime + finish.

relevant_findings.topic: Porch ceiling RP is condition-driven with substrate material as secondary driver
relevant_findings.finding: Like soffit RP, porch ceiling RP prep is primarily condition-driven: sound paint requires wash + scuff only, chalking requires chalk remediation + primer, failing paint requires scrape + feather + spot/full prime, peeling requires heavy scrape + feather + full prime. Substrate material still matters for primer chemistry on exposed areas: bare wood needs acrylic stain-block primer, bare fiber cement needs alkali-resistant primer. NC-specific tasks NOT applicable in RP: TSK_PRCH_SEAL_CUT_EDGES (fiber cement cut edge sealing — already done on NC installation), TSK_PRCH_SPOT_PRIME_KNOTS (bare wood tannin — knots were sealed during original NC).

relevant_findings.topic: Four exterior RP substrate states apply to porch ceiling
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior RP uses 4 substrate states: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (most common RP state — sheltered surface), SS_EXT_CHALKING (less common on porch ceiling than siding — sheltered from UV, but occurs on south/west-facing porches), SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (cracking at panel joints and ceiling-to-fascia/wall junctions), SS_EXT_PEELING (active coating lifting — often at moisture intrusion points from roof above). Maps to GOOD/FAIR/POOR condition scale for prep intensity modifier.

relevant_findings.topic: ALL porch ceiling work is overhead — constant productivity penalty on every task
relevant_findings.finding: Porch ceiling painting is 100% overhead work identical to soffit. NC spec baked overhead penalty into base rates (~25-35% reduction from vertical baselines). RP must follow the same pattern. Height modifier (FAC_EXT_ACCESS) stacks ON TOP of overhead-adjusted base rates. Porch ceilings are typically at 8-10 ft (ground or step ladder access) — LOWER than soffit (16+ ft). This means FAC_EXT_ACCESS ground (1.00) or ladder (1.35) is most common, vs soffit where ladder/scaffold is typical.

relevant_findings.topic: Mildew/algae is the #1 degradation mechanism for porch ceiling — same as soffit
relevant_findings.finding: Porch ceiling is sheltered from direct UV and rain by the porch roof above, making mildew/algae the primary degradation concern — identical to soffit. Sheltered, shaded, damp conditions under porch roofs are ideal for biological growth. Mildew must be treated with biocide BEFORE painting — painting over mildew guarantees adhesion failure. Mildew-resistant paint formulation with mildewcide additive recommended for all porch ceiling RP.

relevant_findings.topic: Spray is ALWAYS eligible on porch ceiling — no vent constraint
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike soffit, porch ceilings have no vent openings (attic ventilation is through soffit vents, ridge vents, or gable vents — NOT porch ceiling). Spray is always eligible regardless of panel type. This simplifies application method selection: both brush_roll and spray are unconditionally available. spray_backroll is NOT valid (overhead back-rolling is impractical — same as soffit/NC).

relevant_findings.topic: Beadboard and T&G are common decorative porch ceiling materials requiring brush-back
relevant_findings.finding: Porch ceilings are frequently decorative with visible T&G boards or beadboard panels. Beadboard is more common on porch ceilings than soffit (decorative intent). T&G and beadboard groove joints require brush-back when spray coating to work paint into grooves. Panel joint complexity modifier (1.20x) applies to brush/roll application tasks on T&G and beadboard. Solid panel has no joint penalty (1.00x).

relevant_findings.topic: Ceiling fans and pendant lights are more common on porch ceiling than soffit fixtures
relevant_findings.finding: Porch ceilings have more and more complex ceiling-mounted fixtures: ceiling fans (with blade removal), pendant lights, recessed cans, and sometimes outdoor chandeliers. Masking is more time-intensive than soffit fixtures. NC spec rated 8 EA/hr for porch ceiling fixtures vs 10 EA/hr for soffit. RP masking should match NC rate — fixtures are installed and operational in both contexts.

relevant_findings.topic: Porch furniture protection replaces landscape protection
relevant_findings.finding: Porch ceilings are above porch floors with furniture. Instead of landscape/hardscape protection (soffit), porch ceiling RP requires: (1) porch floor protection (canvas drops — critical for overhead drips and scraping debris), (2) porch furniture cover/removal (move or cover furniture). Porch floor protection is the primary ground protection zone (always required). Furniture protection is conditional on presence.

relevant_findings.topic: Low-pressure wash replaces power wash — NEVER power wash porch ceiling
relevant_findings.finding: Same prohibition as soffit and NC porch ceiling: NO power washing. Low-pressure garden hose rinse (500-800 PSI max, fan tip) with soft brush and mildew-removal detergent. Allow 24-48 hr dry time (overhead surfaces dry slower — no gravity drainage and limited airflow). Lower pressure than trim wash due to panel edge sensitivity.

relevant_findings.topic: Condition assessment mandatory before porch ceiling RP
relevant_findings.finding: Multi-point assessment required: (1) Visual condition inspection — scan for chalking, cracking, peeling, mildew/algae, moisture staining; (2) Adhesion test — ASTM D3359 cross-hatch tape test; (3) Mildew/algae assessment — porch ceiling priority check (sheltered damp surface); (4) Moisture probe on wood panels at joints and near roof penetrations (MC > 15% = stop work); (5) Caulk condition at panel joints and ceiling-to-fascia/wall junctions.

relevant_findings.topic: EPA RRP applies to pre-1978 homes — overhead scraping is HIGH RISK
relevant_findings.finding: Pre-1978 porch ceilings may contain lead paint. Overhead scraping sends lead-contaminated debris directly onto crew and porch floor below via gravity. EPA RRP containment required: 6-mil poly extending 10 ft from structure perimeter. Wet scraping methods mandatory. HEPA vacuum cleanup. Same protocol as soffit RP RRP.
relevant_findings.source: EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745; SF_SOFFIT_EXT_RP_v1/research.json RF-010
